byline: By the PawRoute relocation team · reviewed by our IPATA-certified specialists · updated June 2026.

key_facts.answer: Relocating a pet from Dubai costs roughly AED 8,000–14,000 for the shortest routes (e.g. India) and AED 25,000–35,000+ for the hardest (Australia, Singapore), with most standard routes — UK, EU, USA — landing around AED 13,800–22,000. The three things that move the price are your pet's size, the destination's rules, and the season.
key_facts.source_authority: PawRoute cost model + MOCCAE / destination authorities

sections.heading: The short answer
paragraphs: Pet relocation from Dubai is not one price — it's a range that depends almost entirely on where you're going and how big your pet is. The cheapest moves are short hops like India (from about AED 8,000); the most expensive are Australia and Singapore (AED 25,000–35,000+), because of rabies titer tests and mandatory quarantine.

The counter-intuitive part: distance isn't the main driver. A move to nearby India is cheaper than to the EU, and Australia costs more than the USA not because it's further, but because its rules are stricter. Rules, size and season set the price — not the map.

sections.heading: Pet relocation cost from Dubai, by route (2026)
sections.intro: Typical all-in ranges for a standard move. Where you land depends on your pet's size and the airline; the hardest routes are higher because of titer tests and quarantine.
sections.note: Ranges from the PawRoute cost model, last verified June 2026. Every route also shares the same UAE-side base costs (vet, microchip, MOCCAE export, IATA crate).

sections.heading: The 3 things that actually drive your price
paragraphs: 1. Your pet's size. Airlines charge by the higher of actual weight or volumetric (crate) weight. A large dog in a big IATA crate can cost AED 1,500+ more in air freight than its kilos suggest — the single biggest swing within a route.

2. The destination's rules. No-quarantine routes (UK, EU, USA, Canada) are cheaper and faster. Routes that demand a rabies titer test and quarantine (Australia, Singapore) cost 2–3× and take months, not weeks.

3. The season. From roughly May to September, the UAE summer heat embargo means many airlines restrict or refuse pet cargo — which can delay a move by weeks regardless of route, and occasionally narrows you to pricier airlines.

sections.heading: The hidden cost nobody quotes you
sections.body: Getting the paperwork wrong is the real budget risk. A rejected health certificate or a missed timing window can add AED 5,000+ in customs delays and re-inspections — far more than any service fee. The cheapest quote that cuts corners on documents isn't cheap.

faqs.q: What's the cheapest country to relocate a pet to from Dubai?
faqs.a: Among common routes, India is typically the cheapest (from about AED 8,000) because it's a short flight with no quarantine. 'Cheapest' depends on your pet's size and the season, though.

faqs.q: Why is Australia so much more expensive?
faqs.a: Australia requires a rabies titer test, a 180-day wait afterwards, and quarantine on arrival. Those add cost and months of time — which is why it runs AED 25,000–35,000+, not because it's further away.

faqs.q: Does my pet's size really change the price that much?
faqs.a: Yes. Airlines charge by crate volume or actual weight, whichever is higher, so a large dog in a big crate can add AED 1,500+ in air freight versus a small pet on the same route.

faqs.q: Will it cost more in summer?
faqs.a: It can take longer, and that can cost more. From May to September the UAE heat embargo restricts pet cargo on many airlines, which may delay your move or limit you to pricier carriers.

faqs.q: Is the cheapest quote the best?
faqs.a: Not if it skips checks. A wrong vet or mistimed treatment can mean a rejected entry and AED 5,000+ in delays. Transparent, correctly-sequenced paperwork is what actually saves money.
